observations: A solid black low-domed shape sits on a black ground strip at the bottom of a flat teal field, with four stubby leg forms visible beneath it and a small rounded head extension at the right.

A single yellow spiral eye sits near the right end of the black form, and yellow zigzag and wave lines radiate outward from the top and sides of the dome in an arc spanning roughly the upper two-thirds of the image.
The teal field above is unbroken except for the radiating yellow lines, leaving a large open expanse of flat color that makes the black silhouette read as low and grounded.
reading: A black silhouette presses close to the ground while yellow lines fan outward from its back like signals or heat. The single spiral eye is the only mark that breaks the form's solid darkness, giving it an odd alertness. The wide empty teal above reads as quiet or distance. The image feels still and charged at once — a slow thing that nonetheless seems to be emitting something.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between nnxyz nnotb #102 — a dense, many-colored composition — and nnxyz nnotb #104, which uses a dark starfield. The spare two-color scheme and single silhouetted form contrast strongly with immediate title neighbor #102.

lookingQuestion: Where exactly do the radiating yellow lines begin relative to the black form — do they emerge from the outline, hover just above it, or overlap it — and what does that gap or contact do to how the two elements relate?
ambiguities: The black ground strip and the black silhouette merge at the base, making it unclear whether the form rests on a surface or is part of it.
